stem: PRINCE2 groups its defined management products into which three types?
answer: Baselines, reports and records
distractors: Baselines, registers and logs
Plans, reports and registers
Baselines, registers and reports
Records, logs and reports
Products, reports and records
Baselines, plans and logs
explanation: The manual sorts the defined management products into baselines, reports and records. The registers and logs are all records, collected together in the project log, so they are not a separate type.

stem: What makes a baseline management product different from the other types?
answer: It defines an aspect of the project and, once approved, becomes subject to change control
distractors: It records the current status of an aspect of the project as that status changes
It gives a snapshot of status at the intervals the project board defines
It summarizes the quality activities planned for each product, and is held by project assurance
It captures informal events and actions that no other product records
It is created only during the initiating a project process, and then approved by the board
It is approved by project assurance rather than by the project board
explanation: Baselines define aspects of the project — the business case, the plans, the product descriptions, the project brief, the project initiation documentation, the project product description and the work package description. Once approved, any change to one of them has to go through change control.

stem: Which statement correctly contrasts reports with records?
answer: A report is a snapshot of certain aspects of the project, whereas a record maintains changing information
distractors: A report is dynamic and updated continuously, whereas a record is fixed once approved
A report is subject to change control once approved, whereas a record is not
A report is created only at the end of a stage, whereas a record is created only at project close
A report is held in the project log, whereas a record is a type of baseline
A report defines an aspect of the project, whereas a record defines acceptance criteria
A report is produced by project assurance, whereas a record is produced by the project board
explanation: Reports give a snapshot of status, which is why they are produced at points in time such as a checkpoint or a stage boundary. Records are dynamic: the registers and logs hold the current and historic record of progress, and together they make up the project log.

stem: What is the purpose of the business case?
answer: To document the justification for the project, based on estimated costs against expected benefits
distractors: To record the reasons for the project and the chosen option in the project mandate
To define the project's scope, objectives and acceptance criteria in one document
To summarize the project's costs and schedule so that progress can be measured
To set out the benefits and the reviews that will confirm they were realized
To obtain the project board's authorization to proceed to the next stage
To record the actual costs and benefits achieved once the project has closed
explanation: The business case documents the justification from estimated costs, expected benefits and the risks that offset them, and it outlines how and when the benefits can be measured. The benefits management approach, not the business case, defines the benefits reviews that confirm realization.

stem: Which heading of the business case compares the aggregated benefits and dis-benefits with the project costs and ongoing operational costs to establish the value of the project as an investment?
answer: Investment appraisal
distractors: Business options
Expected benefits and dis-benefits
Costs
Reasons
Executive summary
Major risks
explanation: Investment appraisal is the section that weighs benefits and dis-benefits against project costs and ongoing incremental operations and maintenance costs. Business options holds the analysis and reasoned recommendation between options, and costs simply summarizes the cost figures and their funding arrangements.

stem: How do the outline and full business cases differ in where they are produced?
answer: The outline is produced in starting up a project, while the full business case is created in initiating a project
distractors: The outline business case is produced in initiating a project and the full business case in managing a stage boundary
The outline business case is produced by the project board and the full business case by the project manager
The outline business case is produced in directing a project and the full business case in closing a project
The outline business case is a stand-alone document and the full business case replaces the project brief
The outline business case is created by project assurance and the full business case by the project executive
The outline business case is optional and the full business case is mandatory only where a programme requires it
explanation: The project manager and project executive produce the outline business case during starting up a project, and it becomes part of the project brief. The project manager then updates it in initiating a project, where the full business case is created as part of the project initiation documentation.

stem: A team manager needs to tell the project manager how a work package is progressing, as often as the work package itself specifies. Which management product is used?
answer: The checkpoint report
distractors: The highlight report
The exception report
The end stage report
The issue report
The work package description
The daily log
explanation: A checkpoint report moves status information from the team manager to the project manager about a work package, and the work package itself sets the reporting frequency. The highlight report is the project manager's report to the board on the stage.

stem: Who creates a checkpoint report, and in which process?
answer: The team manager, in managing product delivery
distractors: The project manager, in controlling a stage
The project manager, in managing a stage boundary
The project board, in directing a project
The team manager, in controlling a stage
Project assurance, in managing product delivery
The project manager, in initiating a project
explanation: The team manager creates the checkpoint report while managing product delivery, and the project manager reviews it in controlling a stage. The project manager's equivalent report upwards is the highlight report.

stem: An end project report reviews how the project performed against what?
answer: The version of the initiation documentation that authorized the project
distractors: The business case as it stood at the end of the last stage
The stage plan for the final stage of the project
The project brief approved at the end of starting up a project
The project product description approved by the project board
The benefits management approach agreed with the business
The project mandate supplied by the business at the outset
explanation: The end project report measures the project against the version of the project initiation documentation that authorized it, which is why that document is baselined. Comparing actuals with the business case baseline is part of closing a project, but the report's stated reference point is the authorizing PID.

stem: Which statement about the creation and review of the end project report is correct?
answer: The project manager creates it in closing a project, assurance confirms it, and the board reviews it
distractors: The project manager creates it in managing a stage boundary, and the project board reviews it there
The team manager creates it in managing product delivery, and project assurance confirms it
The project board creates it in directing a project, and the project manager confirms it
The project manager creates it in controlling a stage, and the board reviews it at the next stage boundary
Project assurance creates it, and the project executive approves it, in the final stage
The project manager creates it in initiating a project, and the board approves it alongside the PID
explanation: The end project report is a closing a project product: the project manager writes it, project assurance confirms it, and the board reviews it while directing the project. Creating a report at a stage boundary is the end stage report instead.

stem: What does the summary of follow-on action recommendations in an end project report contain?
answer: The post-project actions to be taken by the business or by the supplier
distractors: The actions the project manager must complete before the final stage can close
The requests for change that were raised during the project and remain undecided
The lessons that will be carried forward into the next stage of the project
The quality activities still outstanding at the point of handover
The risks that have been transferred to the business at project closure
The recommendations for changes to the project initiation documentation
explanation: Follow-on action recommendations are the post-project actions handed to the business or the supplier, since the project team will no longer be in place to carry them out. Unfinished project work and open requests for change have to be settled before closure, not listed as follow-on actions.

stem: What is the purpose of an end stage report?
answer: To summarize progress and the overall project situation, and to give the board enough information to decide
distractors: To record how the project performed against the project initiation documentation that authorized it
To inform the board that the stage plan is forecast to exceed its tolerances, with options
To report the status of each work package to the project manager, at an agreed frequency
To give the board a summary of stage status at intervals it has defined, and a forecast
To hand formal responsibility for a set of products to a team manager, and to record their acceptance
To describe the impact of a single issue on the project baseline, and to recommend a decision
explanation: The end stage report exists to support the board's decision at a stage boundary, so it summarizes progress and the project situation and offers what the board needs to choose the next step. Assessing the whole project against the authorizing PID is the end project report's job.

stem: In which process is an end stage report created, and by whom?
answer: Managing a stage boundary, by the project manager
distractors: Controlling a stage, by the project manager
Closing a project, by the project manager
Managing product delivery, by the team manager
Directing a project, by the project board
Initiating a project, by the project manager
Starting up a project, by the project manager and project executive
explanation: The project manager creates the end stage report in managing a stage boundary, alongside the next stage plan, and project assurance confirms it. The board then reviews it in directing a project when deciding whether to authorize the next stage.

stem: Both the end stage report and the end project report contain an executive summary and a summary of follow-on action recommendations. Which heading appears only in the end project report?
answer: A product review covering concessions, off-specifications, project product handover and lessons
distractors: A forecast for the next stage and the project against targets and tolerances, with the options available
A review of the business case and of team performance, with recommendations
A summary of key issues and risks, including requests for change and off-specifications
A review of the stage objectives and the quality activities carried out, with their results
A review of the phased handover of products during the stage, with dates and owners
An executive summary written as the project manager's report, with the board's comments
explanation: The end project report adds a product review, which looks back over concessions, off-specifications, project product handover and lessons. A forecast for the next stage exists only in the end stage report, because at project close there is no next stage to forecast.

stem: What is the purpose of an exception report?
answer: To warn the project board when a plan looks set to exceed its tolerances, and to set out options
distractors: To record any deviation from the plan once the stage has closed, and to file it with the log
To ask the project board to approve the next stage plan at a stage boundary
To report the status of a work package to the project manager, and the frequency
To describe an individual issue's impact on the baseline and recommend a decision
To summarize stage status for the board at intervals it defines, and to list the corrective actions
To record the cause of a deviation so that it can be added to the lessons log
explanation: An exception report is raised on a forecast breach of the stage or project plan tolerances and must present options with a recommendation so the board can decide. A single issue with a baseline impact is handled through an issue report instead.

stem: Which statement about who handles an exception report is correct?
answer: The project manager creates it in controlling a stage, and the board responds to it in directing a project
distractors: The team manager creates it in managing product delivery, and the project board responds in directing a project
The project manager creates it in managing a stage boundary, and the project board approves it there
Project assurance creates it and the project board responds in directing a project, in writing
The project manager creates it in controlling a stage, and project assurance decides the response
The project board creates it in directing a project and the business responds to it, in writing
The project manager creates it in closing a project and the board confirms it, in writing
explanation: The project manager raises the exception report while controlling a stage, and the board makes a decision or escalates it to the business while directing the project. The board, not project assurance, owns the response decision.

stem: What does PRINCE2 recommend when an exception is urgent?
answer: That the exception report is oral in the first instance and is then followed up in the agreed format
distractors: That the exception report is deferred until the next stage boundary, and presented to the board then
That the exception report is replaced by an entry in the daily log, and mentioned at the next meeting
That the project manager records the exception in the risk register instead
That the project board is informed only once the exception has been resolved
That the exception is handled as a request for change rather than as an exception
That the project manager issues the report only after updating the business case
explanation: For urgent exceptions the manual recommends giving the report orally first, so the board can act quickly, then following it up in the agreed format. Deferring to a stage boundary would defeat the purpose of escalating a forecast tolerance breach.

stem: What is the purpose of a highlight report?
answer: To give the project board, and possibly others, a summary of stage status at intervals it defines
distractors: To give the project manager a summary of each work package's status at intervals set in the work package
To inform the board that the stage is forecast to exceed its tolerances, with options and a recommendation
To summarize the whole project's performance against the authorizing PID at closure
To review the business case and confirm that the project remains justified
To record the quality activities planned and completed during the stage
To give the team manager formal authorization to begin a work package
explanation: The highlight report is the project manager's regular summary of stage status for the board, at whatever interval the board chooses. The checkpoint report is the equivalent flow from team manager to project manager about a work package.

stem: Who creates a highlight report and who confirms it?
answer: The project manager creates it and project assurance confirms it
distractors: The team manager creates it and the project manager confirms it
The project board creates it and project assurance confirms it
The project manager creates it and the project board confirms it
Project support creates it and the project manager confirms it
The project executive creates it and the senior user confirms it
Project assurance creates it and the project board confirms it
explanation: The project manager creates the highlight report in controlling a stage, project assurance confirms it, and the board reviews it in directing a project. The project board receives the report but does not write or confirm it.

stem: A highlight report has a section on stage and project tolerance status, while a checkpoint report has one on work package tolerance status. What is the difference?
answer: The highlight report covers stage and project tolerances, whereas the checkpoint report covers work package tolerances
distractors: The highlight report covers only time tolerances, whereas the checkpoint report covers time, cost and scope
The highlight report reports the risk budget, whereas the checkpoint report reports the change budget
The highlight report reports the board's tolerances, whereas the checkpoint report reports the business's risk appetite
The highlight report reports tolerances at project closure, whereas the checkpoint report reports them during the stage
The highlight report reports product quality tolerances, whereas the checkpoint report reports stage tolerances
The highlight report reports tolerances set by the team manager, whereas the checkpoint report reports those set by the board
explanation: Each report measures against the level of plan that its reader is accountable for. The highlight report compares stage and project performance with the stage and project tolerances, and the checkpoint report compares work package performance with the tolerances set in that work package.

stem: What is the purpose of an issue report?
answer: To set out how an issue affects the baseline, suggest ways of resolving it, and recommend action
distractors: To log every issue raised during the project, with its status, date of closure
To inform the board that the stage plan is forecast to exceed its tolerances, with options
To record the lessons arising from an issue for use by future projects, the programme
To authorize a change to the project baseline on the board's behalf, record it
To capture informal events and actions that no other product records, such as meetings and calls
To summarize the quality activities associated with an affected product, its reviews
explanation: The issue report analyzes the baseline impact and sets out options with a recommendation so a decision can be taken. Logging every issue with its status and closure date is the purpose of the issue register.

stem: Which statement about issue reports and the issue register is correct?
answer: Not every entry in the issue register needs a separately documented issue report
distractors: Every entry in the issue register must have its own issue report
An issue report replaces the need for an issue register on small projects
Issue reports are added to the issue register only once the issue is closed
The issue register holds only those issues for which an issue report exists
An issue report is created by the project board for the issues it escalates
Issue reports are optional, but a project log may not contain an issue register
explanation: The issue register logs every issue, but a full issue report is only needed where the impact has to be analyzed and a decision recommended. Its format is defined in the issue management approach, and many register entries will never need one.

stem: What does the decision section of an issue report record when the issue is an off-specification?
answer: That it was accepted, with a summary of the concession granted
distractors: The options available and the effect of each on the business case and risks
The project manager's or team manager's recommended course of action
The severity and priority assigned to the issue when it was graded
The date the issue was first logged and the product it affects
The person who raised the issue and their relationship to the product
The escalation of the issue to the project board for a decision
explanation: The decision section records what was decided, and for an off-specification that means recording that it was accepted with a summary of the concession. The options and the recommendation are separate sections that feed that decision.

stem: What is the purpose of a lessons report?
answer: To pass on what has been learned and prompt action so the learning changes how work is done
distractors: To record every lesson identified during the project in a single repository
To describe how the project performed against the authorizing PID
To set out the actions the business must take after the project closes
To summarize the quality activities planned and carried out during a stage
To provide the project board with a summary of stage status, and the forecast for the next stage
To define the lessons that will be reviewed at the next stage boundary
explanation: A lessons report exists to share learning and prompt action so that it changes how the organization works. Keeping the running record of lessons is the job of the lessons log.

stem: Why might a single project produce several lessons reports?
answer: Because different organizations, such as the user and the supplier, may each need their own
distractors: Because one report is required for each stage of the project, and one for each work package
Because the project board and the project manager must report separately
Because each lesson must be reported to the business layer individually
Because lessons reports replace the lessons log once a stage closes
Because project assurance must confirm a separate report for each lesson
Because a report is needed for every work package delivered by a supplier
explanation: The manual says it may be appropriate and necessary for there to be several lessons reports specific to a particular organization, naming the user, supplier and business as examples. The number of reports follows the organizations involved, not the number of stages or lessons.

stem: What do the project manager and project executive do with lessons reports during starting up a project?
answer: Review lessons reports from other projects and other organizations
distractors: Create the project's lessons report for the initiation stage
Confirm that lessons and follow-on actions have been assigned
Approve the lessons log on behalf of the project board
Escalate all previous lessons to the business layer for a decision
Update the end project report with lessons drawn from the mandate
Review the lessons log only once the project has closed
explanation: Starting up a project is where previous lessons are reviewed by the project manager and project executive, including lessons from other organizations, so that they can shape the project's approaches and plans. Confirming that lessons and follow-on actions are assigned is project assurance's role in closing a project.

stem: What is the purpose of a plan?
answer: To propose how and when the project will be performed, and provide a baseline for progress
distractors: To define the quality methods and acceptance criteria for each product
To authorize a team manager to begin work on a set of products, and to agree the tolerances
To record the actual progress of the stage against its tolerances
To describe the business justification for the project and its benefits
To list all the products required for a plan and the status of each
To summarize the lessons that have been incorporated into the stage
explanation: A plan is a proposal for how the work will be done, and once approved it becomes the baseline against which progress is measured and issues are assessed. Authorizing a team manager to start work is done through a work package description.

stem: The budget section of a plan shows the project costs including which two budgets?
answer: The risk budget and the change budget
distractors: The stage budget and the team budget
The contingency budget and the benefits budget
The capital budget and the operational budget
The supplier budget and the assurance budget
The cost budget and the time budget
The project budget and the programme budget
explanation: The plan's budget covers project costs and explicitly includes the risk budget and the change budget. Benefits funding and the ongoing operational costs are treated in the business case, not as a second budget inside the plan.

stem: Which statement about who creates and approves plans is correct?
answer: The team manager creates the team plan in managing product delivery, and the project manager approves it in controlling a stage
distractors: The project manager creates the team plan in controlling a stage, and the team manager approves it in managing product delivery
The project board creates the stage plan in directing a project, and the project manager approves it
The project manager creates the project plan in starting up a project, and the board approves it there
The team manager creates the stage plan in managing a stage boundary, and the board approves it
The project manager creates the team plan in managing a stage boundary, and project assurance approves it
The project board creates the project plan in initiating a project, and the executive approves it
explanation: The team manager creates and updates the team plan while managing product delivery, and the project manager approves and checks it in controlling a stage. The project plan is created by the project manager in initiating a project, and stage plans by the project manager at a stage boundary.

stem: Which management product sets out a product's purpose, composition, what it is derived from and its quality specifications, and is produced as soon as the need for the product is identified?
answer: The product description
distractors: The quality register
The work package description
The product register
The product breakdown structure
The quality management approach
The stage plan
explanation: A product description sets out the product's purpose, its composition, what it is derived from and its quality specifications, and is produced at planning time as soon as the need is identified. Recording quality activities and results is the quality register's job.

stem: What does the quality tolerance section of a product description define?
answer: The limits within which a product's key quality specifications may vary
distractors: The functional and non-functional requirements the product must meet, with their measures
The quality methods used to check that the product meets its specification
The permissible deviation from the stage's cost and time targets
The people who will produce, review and accept the product
The skills, facilities and equipment needed to develop the product
The standards and procedures the project must apply to achieve quality
explanation: Quality tolerance is the band within which key quality specifications may vary and remain acceptable. Quality specifications are the requirements and their measures, and the quality methods are the verification, test and inspection techniques used to check them.

stem: What is the purpose of the project brief?
answer: To establish a complete and reliable basis on which the project can be initiated
distractors: To justify the project and explain why the chosen business option was selected
To act as the contract between the project manager and the project board
To authorize the project manager to start the first stage of delivery
To record the project's products, activities, resources and people as a baseline
To summarize how the project performed against the authorizing documentation
To define the responsibilities of each member of the project board
explanation: The project brief is the foundation document that starting up a project produces so that initiation can begin on a firm footing. The project initiation documentation, together with the stage plan, is what forms the contract with the board.

stem: Which of these is NOT part of the project brief?
answer: The full business case
distractors: The outline business case
The project product description
The project approach
explanation: The project brief carries the outline business case, not the full one; the full business case is created during initiating a project and becomes part of the project initiation documentation. The project product description and project approach, by contrast, are both project brief contents.

stem: What happens to the project brief once the project is being initiated?
answer: The project manager reviews it in initiating the project, and it then forms part of the PID
distractors: It is archived once the PID is approved and is not referred to again
It is replaced by the project mandate, which the board re-approves
It becomes the project plan, against which progress is measured, and the stage plans are derived
It is updated at every stage boundary and reissued to the board, and to the business layer
It is confirmed by project assurance at project closure, and the board is told of it
It stays a separate baseline that the PID must not duplicate, and the manager must not amend
explanation: The project brief is reviewed by the project manager during initiating a project, after which it is absorbed into the project initiation documentation rather than living on as a separate document. That is why the brief is only shown as produced in starting up a project and approved in directing a project.

stem: The project initiation documentation, together with which other product, forms the contract between the project manager and the project board?
answer: The stage plan
distractors: The project plan
The project brief
The business case
The project product description
The end stage report
The work package description
explanation: The project initiation documentation gives the direction and scope of the project and, together with the stage plan, forms the contract between the project manager and the board. The project plan sits inside the PID rather than alongside it.

stem: Which of these is one of the three primary uses of the project initiation documentation?
answer: The one place newcomers can look to understand the project
distractors: To authorize each work package before delivery begins
To record the actual costs and benefits achieved at project close
To set out the quality methods for every product in the project
To summarize stage status for the board at intervals it defines
To justify the project to the business layer at each stage boundary
To record issues and their impact on the project baseline
explanation: The three uses are to ensure a sound basis before the board commits, to act as the base document for assessing progress, issues and viability, and to be a single source of reference for those joining the temporary organization. Work packages are authorized by a work package description.

stem: Which management approach covers market engagement, procurement and contract management?
answer: The commercial management approach
distractors: The change management approach
The benefits management approach
The communication management approach
The digital and data management approach
The sustainability management approach
The issue management approach
explanation: The commercial management approach describes how the project will secure, service and maintain its commercial agreements, which is where market engagement, procurement and contract management sit. The change management approach is about moving the business to its target organizational state.

stem: Which statement about the use of the project initiation documentation during delivery is correct?
answer: The team manager reviews it in managing delivery, and work package descriptions may refer to it
distractors: The team manager approves it in managing product delivery before work starts
It is no longer used once the first stage plan has been approved, and the board then archives it
The team manager updates it at the end of every work package, and the board approves each update
It is reissued in full at every stage boundary by project assurance
The project board reviews it in managing product delivery, and the team manager approves the review
It is replaced by the business case once delivery begins, and the board archives the original
explanation: The PID remains a live reference throughout delivery: the team manager reviews it while managing product delivery, and the management approaches it contains may be referenced in a work package description. Only the project manager updates it, and only in specific processes such as managing a stage boundary.

stem: Which management product is a changing record of issues, lessons, products, quality, risk and informal events, often held as a collection of logs and registers?
answer: The project log
distractors: The project brief
The stage plan
The business case
The highlight report
The end project report
The project initiation documentation
explanation: The project log is dynamic, holding the current and historic record of issues, lessons, products, quality, risk and informal events. Its registers and logs are records, not baselines, so approved baselines are kept outside it.

stem: What is the purpose of the lessons log?
answer: To hold the lessons captured, for this project or later projects
distractors: To describe each lesson in enough detail to trigger action across the organization
To record the quality activities from which each lesson was derived
To log the issues that gave rise to lessons, together with their status
To record the decisions taken about which lessons to escalate
To hold the follow-on actions the business must complete after closure
To summarize the lessons that have been incorporated into the current plan
explanation: The lessons log is the repository for lessons, including lessons that originate outside the project and feed into its approaches and plans. Triggering action so that lessons change the way the organization works is the purpose of the lessons report.

stem: Which register lists the products a plan requires, with each product's status, current version and the dates its description was approved and the product accepted?
answer: The product register
distractors: The quality register
The issue register
The risk register
The lessons log
The daily log
The product breakdown structure
explanation: The product register lists the products required for a plan with their status and current version, together with the dates of product description approval and product acceptance. Quality activities and their results are held in the quality register instead.

stem: The quality register summarizes all quality management activities that are planned or have occurred. Which two parties use it as part of reviewing progress?
answer: The project manager and project assurance
distractors: The project board and the project executive
The team manager and project support
The senior user and the senior supplier
The project manager and the team manager
Project assurance and the business layer
The project board and the change authority
explanation: The manual states that the quality register is used by the project manager and project assurance as part of reviewing progress. It holds the quality activities for each product, so it feeds directly into the reviews those two roles carry out.

stem: Which two fields of the risk register estimate when a risk might occur and how quickly it would affect objectives?
answer: Proximity and velocity
distractors: Probability and impact
Planned residual probability and impact
Risk owner and risk action owner
Probability and proximity
Impact and velocity
Risk identifier and risk description
explanation: Proximity estimates how soon a risk might occur, and velocity estimates how quickly it would affect objectives if it did. Probability and impact are the minimum qualitative assessment of likelihood and size, not of timing.

stem: Which statement about the daily log is correct?
answer: It takes informal issues, actions and events that no other product captures, and can hold early risks
distractors: It records every issue raised, replaces the issue register on small projects, and is held by the manager
It is held by the project board, records the decisions taken at board meetings, and is signed by the executive
It is a single log, which team managers are not permitted to keep separately, and which the board reviews
It holds the quality activities planned for each work package, the results, and the reviewers' names
It is created in initiating a project, closed at the first stage boundary, and archived by project support
It records the lessons that will feed into the end project report, the lessons report
explanation: The daily log can act as the project manager's diary for informal issues, actions and significant events, and it is created during starting up a project when the other registers do not yet exist. There may be more than one, since team managers may keep one for their work packages.

stem: What is the purpose of the project product description?
answer: To set out the project's major products, with quality expectations and acceptance criteria
distractors: To describe each product's composition, quality specifications and quality tolerance
To set out the work, tolerances and reporting arrangements for a work package
To provide a full and firm foundation for the initiation of the project
To record the user's quality expectations for each stage of the project
To define the products to be delivered in a stage and their interdependencies
To summarize the quality activities to be carried out for each major product
explanation: The project product description covers the project's major products, the user's quality expectations, the acceptance criteria and how acceptance will be confirmed. Describing an individual product's composition and quality specifications is the job of a product description.

stem: What is the acceptance criteria section of the project product description?
answer: A ranked list of conditions the products must satisfy to be accepted
distractors: A description of the quality expected of the products and the standards to be applied
The means by which acceptance will be confirmed and who will decide
The tolerances that apply to the acceptance criteria
A description of the major products the project will deliver
The source the products are based on, such as an existing system
The functional and non-functional requirements for each product
explanation: Acceptance criteria are a prioritized list that the products must meet for the user to accept them. The user's quality expectations describe the quality expected and the standards to apply, while acceptance methods and responsibilities cover how and by whom acceptance is confirmed.

stem: During closing a project, what do the project manager and project assurance each do with the project product description?
answer: The project manager reviews it and project assurance confirms it
distractors: The project manager updates it and project assurance approves it
The project manager creates it and the project board approves it
The project manager reviews it and the project board confirms it
Project assurance reviews it and the project manager confirms it
The project board reviews it and the project executive confirms it
The project manager confirms it and project assurance reviews it
explanation: At closure the project manager reviews the project product description and project assurance confirms it, which is how the team satisfies itself that the acceptance criteria have been met. Approval belongs to the board, but earlier in the lifecycle, in directing a project.

stem: Which management product is the vehicle for delegating work to a team manager or team member, describing what is to be produced and how, with tolerances and reporting arrangements?
answer: The work package description
distractors: The product description
The stage plan
The team plan
The checkpoint report
The project plan
The project product description
explanation: The work package description is the vehicle for delegating work, describing what is to be produced and how, with tolerances and reporting arrangements. Progress against it comes back through checkpoint reports.

stem: What does the agreement section of a work package description record?
answer: The initial authorization and final completion of the work package by the project and team managers
distractors: The team manager's acceptance of the products on behalf of the user, and the project manager's approval
The project board's approval of the products within the work package, and the date of the approval
The contract between the customer organization and the supplier, and the terms of payment for the work
The quality methods agreed for checking the products, and the people who will apply each of the methods
The constraints on the work, such as authorized hours and security measures
The identity of whoever will approve each completed product, and the date by which they must do so
explanation: The agreement section is the record of the work package being authorized at the start and completed at the end, made between the project manager and the team manager. Naming who approves the completed products is a separate approval section.

stem: When may a work package description be given orally?
answer: When the work is done by a team working directly under the project manager, though writing is recommended
distractors: When the work is being performed by a supplier under a contract with the customer organization
When the project board has delegated the work package to the project manager
When the work package has no tolerances and no products to deliver
When the project is using an iterative-incremental delivery method, and the team works in sprints each fortnight
When the products are to be approved by project assurance rather than the board
Never, because a work package description must always be a formal written instruction
explanation: Where a team works directly under the project manager, the description may be an oral instruction, though writing it down avoids misunderstanding and supports performance assessment. Where a supplier works under contract, a formal written instruction matching the contract standards is needed.
